name: UK inflation & rates
summary: Bank Rate 4% after the 5 Nov rise; CPI 3.5% in September, Bank expects about 5% by mid-2027; October CPI due 18 Nov
state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in the 12 months to September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov on an 8–1 vote and projects inflation of about 5% by mid-2027 (Business News Today). No further rate decision is due before December; October CPI is published on 18 Nov, and a print above 4% would cross the Alert line.
for_you: Households with variable-rate or expiring fixed mortgages are exposed to higher borrowing costs, and rising prices squeeze real incomes. The Bank of England and ONS publish the official figures.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 3.5% (Sep) within the 2.5–4.0% band, and BoE reversed course with a rise to 4% on 5 Nov

sources.title: Business News Today — Bank of England raises interest rate to 4% as UK inflation heads towards 5%

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
